earlier_scan.source_named: Heath, David Mark. 2020. u̱s-Saare̱: Phonological and Grammar Sketch with a Focus on the Dukku Dialect of u̱s-Saare̱ [uss]. 217pp. (Glottolog ref 587506; no online copy found)

sources.citation: Bendor-Samuel, John, Esther Cressman & Donna Skitch. 1971. The nominal phrase in Duka. Journal of West African Languages 8(2): 59-78.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Only phonological remark is footnote 3 (p. 60): acute/grave mark high/low tone, mid tone unmarked; three level tones (high, mid, low) used throughout for concord elements. Syntactic paper (Eastern dialect focus per Dettweiler 2003).

sources.citation: WALS Online, language Duka (wals_code_duk); Glottolog 5.3 languoid huns1239 and reference 587506; OLAC static page for dud (Wayback 2019/2026).
sources.note: WALS has Duka with only Bendor-Samuel et al. 1973 as source and no stress-chapter datapoints; Glottolog lists 8 descriptive refs (all Heath 2020 or Bendor-Samuel et al. 1971/1973 duplicates); OLAC lists no phonology item for dud beyond these.

sources.citation: Heath, David. 2018. ISO 639-3 change request 2018-014 (split Hun-Saare [dud] into ut-Hun [uth] and us-Saare [uss]), with new-code forms for uss and uth.
sources.note: Nothing on phonology; only cites Dettweiler & Dettweiler 1993 and 2003 as published sources.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Stuart McGill. 2012. The Kainji languages of Northwestern and Central Nigeria. Circulation draft (May 2012). Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation.
sources.note: No stress statement for Hun-Saare. §3.7.2.2 'Linguistic studies of tHun-sSaare' (p. 27): noun phrase described in Bendor-Samuel et al. 1973; Cressman & Skitch (1980) is 'a summary description of the language'; an electronic dictionary of tHun and 'a grammar sketch (Heath n.d.)' exist with the translation project. Tone notes in the volume are for Cinda and Hungwəryə, not Hun-Saare.

sources.citation: Dettweiler, Stephen & Sonia Dettweiler. 2003. Sociolinguistic survey of the Duka (Hun-Saare) people. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2003-014.
sources.note: Nothing on stress or tone. Useful as a bibliography: says Cressman & Skitch contributed 'a 75-item word list along with a list of 128 phrases and clauses and a few notes on Duka phonology and grammar (1974) to the West African Language Data Sheets, Volume 2 (Kropp-Dakubu, ed. 1980)'; most of Cressman & Skitch's notes were lost.
